Privacy Policy

App: Teacher's App (Aplikacja Nauczyciela)
Developer & data controller: Maciej Bernacki
Contact: bernacki.dev@gmail.com
Last updated: August 4, 2026

1. Overview

This Privacy Policy explains what data Teacher's App handles, what never leaves your device, what is sent to external services and why, and how long anything is kept. The app is a planning and storytelling assistant for early-childhood teachers and is intended for adult professional users.

The app has no user accounts. We do not collect your name, e-mail address, or any profile of you. The app's guiding design rule is that children's personal data never leaves your device: pupils' names, dates, notes, and any other identifying details are removed or replaced with neutral labels on the device itself before any request is sent to any service.

2. Data that stays on your device

The following data is stored only on your device, in the app's local database and private storage. It is never uploaded automatically. The only ways any of it can leave the device are the actions you take yourself: exporting or sharing a file, or submitting a content report (§3.8).

  • Pupil profiles — names and your descriptions of each child's educational needs
  • Classes and groups
  • Generated day plans and stories (after generation, the app re-inserts real names locally — the versions containing real names exist only on your device)
  • Downloaded story narration audio and exported story videos
  • Photos you pick as a video background — chosen through the Android system photo picker (the app has no permission to browse your gallery), copied into the app's private storage, and combined into the video entirely on-device
  • App settings and language preferences

Voice dictation, where offered, uses Android's built-in speech recognition. Only the recognized text is used; the app never records, stores, or transmits audio to our servers.

Uninstalling the app deletes all of this local data.

3. What is sent to our server, and why

The app's AI features run through a proxy server operated by the developer on Google Cloud Run in the European Union (region europe-central2, Warsaw). The app never talks to AI providers directly. Every request to the proxy carries: an anonymous device identifier (a random UUID created on installation — it identifies the installation, not you), the app version, and for some requests a Google Play Integrity token used to block abuse. The proxy's logs record technical metadata only (request type, outcome, timing, an anonymized device identifier) — never the content of your requests.

3.1. AI generation (day plans, stories, adaptations)

To generate content, the app sends your lesson parameters and — where you have provided them — descriptions of pupils' educational or developmental needs. These descriptions are what the AI personalises activities against, and they can concern matters such as neurodivergence or behaviour, so please describe only what is needed. Before anything is sent, the app removes names and identifying details on-device and replaces each child with a neutral label (such as "Child A"); responses are checked on-device and rejected if they contain a real name. The descriptions are processed to generate your content and are not stored on our server. Generated stories are written with fictional character names only.

3.2. Story narration (text-to-speech)

When you request narration, the story text — which contains only fictional names — and your chosen voice are sent through the proxy to ElevenLabs, a speech-synthesis provider based in the United States (see §4 on data transfer). The finished audio is downloaded to your device.

3.3. Story illustrations

When you request an illustration, a name-free description of the story is used to generate an image, which is stored in Google Cloud Storage so your device can download it. The image is served from an unguessable link that is not published anywhere by the app, but anyone who has the exact link could open it — do not treat illustration links as private if you share them.

3.4. Purchases and subscriptions

Payments are handled exclusively by Google Play Billing — we never receive your card details, name, or address. After a purchase, the app sends the purchase token issued by Google Play to the proxy, which verifies it with Google and stores in Google Cloud Firestore (EU region): the anonymous device identifier, the purchase token, the product purchased (subscription tier and plan, or a one-time token package), its expiry, and verification timestamps. Google Play also notifies our server directly about subscription state changes (for example a cancellation), so entitlements stay correct.

3.5. Usage limits and token balances

To operate free-tier limits and token economies fairly across reinstalls, the server keeps per-device counters keyed to the anonymous device identifier: how many free generations have been used, and current story/audio token balances.

3.6. Rewarded ads

If you watch a rewarded ad to earn an extra generation, Google AdMob calls our server with a signed confirmation containing the ad event and the anonymous device identifier, which the server verifies and uses to credit the reward.

3.7. Referral programme

If you install the app through someone's referral link, the Google Play install referrer carries their referral code; the app reads only that code from it. Crediting a referral links the new installation's anonymous device identifier to the inviter's anonymous device identifier on our server. Neither identifier can be resolved to a person — no names, contacts, accounts, or Play profile data are collected. Referral requests additionally use Play Integrity checks and per-device caps to prevent farming.

3.8. Content reports

The app includes a "Report this content" option on AI-generated content. Submitting a report uploads: the content type and report category you chose, your optional comment, the reported content itself, language and voice metadata, the app version, and the anonymous device identifier. Reports are the one case where app content is uploaded for a human (not an AI) to review. Privacy protections still apply on the way out: reported stories contain only fictional names by design; in a reported day plan, pupils' real names are replaced with neutral tags on your device before upload; reporting an illustration sends its existing link rather than re-uploading the image. Reports are reviewed by the developer and used for content moderation, as required by Google Play's AI-generated content policy.

4. Service providers

The app relies on the following processors:

Service Purpose What it receives Location
Google Gemini (2.5 Flash) AI text and image generation Anonymized, name-free prompts (§3.1) Via our EU proxy
ElevenLabs, Inc. Story narration (text-to-speech) Name-free story text and voice choice (§3.2) United States
Google AdMob Advertising in the free tier Advertising ID, ad interactions (§6) Per Google's policy
Google Play Billing Payments Handled by Google; we see tokens only (§3.4) Per Google's policy
Google Play Integrity Abuse protection Device/installation integrity signals Per Google's policy
Google Cloud (Run, Firestore, Storage, Logging) Server hosting, storage, logs The server-side data described in §3 EU — europe-central2 (Warsaw)

Narration requests are the one flow processed outside the EEA: ElevenLabs processes the name-free story text in the United States under its data-processing terms, which incorporate EU Standard Contractual Clauses. See also: Google Privacy Policy.

5. How long data is kept

Data Retention
Content of AI requests (prompts, descriptions) Not stored — processed in transit only
Server logs (technical metadata, no request content) 30 days
Purchase and entitlement records For as long as the app is operated — required to keep paid features working and to prevent abuse
Usage counters and token balances For as long as the app is operated
Referral records For as long as the app is operated (fraud prevention)
Content reports Kept as the app's content-moderation record for as long as the app is operated
Story illustrations (cloud copy) Until replaced by a regenerated version, or on request
All local data on your device Until you delete it or uninstall the app

All server-side records are keyed to the anonymous device identifier only. You can request their deletion at any time (§8).

6. Advertising and consent

The free tier shows ads served by Google AdMob. AdMob may collect your device's advertising ID, ad-interaction data, and approximate (country-level) location. On first launch in the EEA/UK the app shows a consent form where you choose between personalized and non-personalized ads; you can change this choice at any time in the app's Settings ("Ad privacy options") or in Android's system settings. Subscribers do not see ads. Details: Google Advertising Policy.

7. Children's data

The app is a professional tool for adult teachers and is not directed at children; we do not knowingly collect personal data from children. The pupil information a teacher enters is the teacher's own professional record: it is stored only on the teacher's device, and as described in §2 and §3, it is never transmitted anywhere in a form that identifies a child. Purchases are tied to the adult teacher's Google Play account.

8. Your rights (GDPR)

Under the GDPR you have the rights of access, rectification, erasure, restriction, objection, and data portability, and the right to lodge a complaint with your supervisory authority (in Poland: UODO).

  • Local data is under your direct control — you can edit or delete it in the app, and uninstalling removes it all.
  • Server-side records are anonymous (a random device identifier; nothing that names you). To have the records for your installation deleted, contact us at bernacki.dev@gmail.com — note that deleting them also removes the entitlement and balance history they carry.
  • Ad-consent withdrawal is available at any time as described in §6.

9. Security

All traffic between the app, the proxy, and service providers uses HTTPS. Local data is protected by Android's app sandbox. Server-side data lives in the EU region; administrative access to it is restricted to the developer and secret-gated; logs never contain request content. No security measure is absolute, but the architecture is designed so that the most sensitive data — anything naming a child — never reaches a server in the first place.

10. Changes to this policy

We may update this policy as the app evolves or the law requires. The current version is always available at this address, with the last-updated date shown above. Material changes will be reflected in the app or its store listing.
